note: Fictional resumes for the under-count and over-count checks. A bad resume has exactly three problems, each serious enough on its own to cost an interview, listed most important first; everything else on it is deliberately clean. A strong resume has none. lines are verbatim resume lines, distinct across a resume's problems.

problems.problem: The latest role ends January 2025 and nothing is listed after it.
problems.why: With nothing listed after the end date, a recruiter reads the candidate as out of the field and screens out before reading the rest.

problems.problem: The Operations Supervisor bullets give no team size, volume, site size or result.
lines: - Supervised the day shift on the warehouse floor
- Assigned pick and pack work to associates
- Checked outbound trailers before they left the dock
problems.why: The latest role is what a recruiter weighs most; with no size and no result anywhere in it, there is nothing to judge the candidate on.

problems.problem: The headline claims a Director of Operations who runs multi-site networks, but the latest role is a shift supervisor at one warehouse.
lines: Director of Operations who runs multi-site distribution networks and leads large warehouse teams.
problems.why: A title or headline the work does not support reads as inflation, and a recruiter stops trusting the rest of the page.
